benefit.name: Alberta Aids to Daily Living (AADL)
benefit.amount: Funding for medical equipment & supplies (you pay a small share)
benefit.summary: Helps pay for equipment and supplies you need for a long-term illness, disability or condition — wheelchairs, hearing aids, breathing supplies and much more.
benefit.note: Covers a wide range of devices. You usually pay 25% (capped per year). Low-income households can have that waived.
benefit.applyText: Open the official page on alberta.ca

detail.about: A provincial program that funds basic medical equipment and supplies for Albertans with a long-term disability, chronic illness or terminal illness — mobility aids, hearing aids, vision aids, breathing equipment, diabetic and ostomy supplies, and more.
steps: See an AADL-authorized health professional (e.g. an OT, audiologist, or specialist) who assesses what you need.
They complete the authorization for the specific equipment.
Get the item from an approved vendor; AADL covers its share directly.
documents: An assessment from an authorized professional for the specific item
tips: You don't apply to a general office. You go through an authorizer (often an OT, physio, or audiologist). Ask your doctor for a referral.
The 25% cost-share is capped each year. Low-income Albertans and people receiving income assistance do not pay it.
detail.time: Depends on the assessment and vendor.

extra.taxNote: You usually pay a 25% cost-share (capped each year) — you do not pay it if you are low-income or receiving income assistance.
